items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: Slam plays on that [Groovin' High]. So he bought that because of Slam.

ctx.x: Yeah, I wanted to ask you perhaps maybe just one last question here and that is you know students hopefully, the students even at our college and perhaps even other colleges, will see these tapes. Tell us a few things that students should know about jazz, other than just the names and dates.

Well the names and dates are things that you latch on to once you get interested in a particular band or a particular musician and so you want to know when this happened, how it happened, etcetera, etcetera. But I think the thing to do is keep your ears open and listen, and listen as much as you can. And the more you listen, the more knowledgeable you become and the more sophisticated in your listening, and you’re able to make judgments and comparisons, and also to understand your taste. Because everyone’s taste…

you to another and then it’s like I had a friend who liked jazz but he wasn’t avidly as into it as myself, and he took Slam Stewart — he loved Slam Stewart singing and bowing the bass at the same time. Everybody kind of could get with that. And because he liked Slam and I played the record of “Groovin’ High” which I spoke of before for him, and Slam plays on that. So he bought that because of Slam. And then he said to me, “Wow, Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie.” So Slam Stewart really opened that other thing up…
